Anya: quick question — saw a user error with request_id=7fb2a3e9 (from the report). What's the fastest way to pull the full request logs + the trace? I searched the console logs UI but didn't see anything obvious.
Liam: if you have a trace_id that's the easiest — Traces UI -> paste id, open related spans. If you only have request_id, try the Logs UI filter first: `request_id:7fb2a3e9` (top-right time selector to last 1h/24h).
Anya: I didn't get a trace id, only the request_id from the frontend. Console logs filter returned nothing though.
Natalie: two quick checks — 1) confirm header name (`x-request-id` vs `request_id`), we log the header as `x-correlation-id` in prod by default. 2) timeframe — client clock and server clock mismatch is common. Try expanding to 24h.
Liam: CLI alternative that's usually faster for me:
```
# find traces by request id (will return trace ids if present)
rcli traces search --query "attributes.request_id:7fb2a3e9" --limit 5
# then inspect logs for a given trace
rcli logs get --trace-id <TRACE_ID> --tail
```
Anya: Nice, I don't have `rcli` set up on this laptop. Any console shortcut to map request->trace?
devex-kim: In the Console, Observability -> Traces -> "Search traces" accepts `attributes.request_id:...`. There's also a helper: Requests page -> paste request id -> tries to map to trace if available. Bookmark: https://console.redwood.ai/docs/observability/lookup-requests
oncall-sre: FYI if the request hit a cached layer or got filtered at the ingress, we may not have the server-side `request_id`. If you can share the exact header/value I can run a backend lookup (I can also check raw ingress logs).
Anya: header name was `x-request-id: 7fb2a3e9`. I tried the Traces search with that attribute and found one trace id: 9c1f4b2a. Thanks!
sre-bot: trace 9c1f4b2a: https://console.redwood.ai/traces/9c1f4b2a (linked)
Liam: once you have the trace link, open the trace and click "Open logs for span" — that jumps to the logs view with the correct time range and filters applied.
Natalie: note on retention/sampling: infra teams sample traces above 1MB or very high QPS endpoints. If you think it was sampled away, let us know the high-level endpoint and approximate time window; we can search raw logs (longer retention) using the ingress request id.
Anya: this is perfect. One last question — is there a cookbook for when console search returns nothing? Steps I should follow before pinging oncall?
devex-kim: short checklist to add to the docs:
- verify header name and exact value (paste)
- expand time window +/- 10m then 1h
- try Traces search with `attributes.request_id:`
- use CLI `rcli traces search` if you have it
- if still missing, paste the timestamp + endpoint + request header in #incidents or DM oncall
I'll add the checklist to the docs page.
Anya: thanks all :thumbsup: saved my morning.
